correctness.rationale: Independently expanded the physicists' Hermite polynomials in u=2πx²: stripping the Gaussian gives every packet member as P(u)=c+u[A(u−3)+Bp(u)] with p(u)=u³−14u²+105u/2−105/2 and c=f(0)≤0. Coefficient matching gives p+α(u−3)=(u−η)(u−z)² with η=14−2z, α=−3z²+28z−105/2 exactly when W(z)=0. W has critical points 3 and 14/3, both of negative value, and opposite signs at 11/2 and 6, so 2<η<3<z. As a direct certificate including negative origin values, weight P(η)/η by z−3 and P(z)/z by 3−η. The terms in A−Bα cancel and the resulting weighted sum is c[(z−3)/η+(3−η)/z]≤0. Nonnegativity at both contacts forces c=0 and A=Bα. Otherwise negativity at one contact, by continuity, forces a strictly larger last-sign radius. In the equality case eventual nonnegativity and nontriviality force B>0; the exhibited polynomial is negative below η and nonnegative from η on, giving the claimed radius and multiplicities. This also handles degree-degenerate cases. Read the SymPy checker and archived log, including R≈0.6009643878548390; no frozen code was executed.
